title: China-to-Indonesia Air-source Heat Pump Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Mandatory energy label (1 to 5 stars) and market-facing declaration
rows.target_requirement: ESDM requires energy labels for applicable air-conditioners and heat pumps using a 1 to 5 star framework. Market-facing labels and documentation should reflect Indonesian reporting format and the current model classification before sale and customs-linked review where applied.
target_standards: ESDM energy label rules for air conditioners and heat pumps
Indonesian model classification and label format notices
rows.china_equivalent: China applies China Energy Label rules and GB-based performance labeling, but the label scales, data schema, and enforcement path differ from Indonesia's star framework.
china_standards: Related GB air-conditioner efficiency labeling notices
rows.gap: The main gap is format and compliance authority mapping: Indonesia requires ESDM-grade labeling that may not align with China domestic label layout or test-cycle assumptions. Product teams should produce Indonesia-specific label text and evidence package.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for products within ESDM-covered categories and before market entry
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory for Chinese energy-label categories; scheme logic not automatically transferable to Indonesia

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Labeling is a likely mandatory gap: Indonesian star-label declarations and filing paths must be prepared locally even if Chinese energy-label data exist.

source.publisher: Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry (ESDM), Indonesia

rows.requirement: Minimum Energy Performance Standard (MEPS) and EER floor
rows.target_requirement: ESDM applies MEPS-type minimum efficiency gates, including minimum EER requirements for the relevant category of heat-pump and air-conditioner products. Importer and technical teams must verify model banding and seasonal versus point metric interpretation before declaration.
target_standards: ESDM MEPS regulation for air conditioners and heat pumps
ESDM monitoring notices for minimum efficiency thresholds
rows.china_equivalent: China uses GB 25454 and related efficiency baselines including COP and SCOP reporting, yet those values may follow different scope and compliance triggers than Indonesian MEPS-EER and category-specific minimum thresholds.
rows.gap: A typical gap is metric comparability: reported EER and seasonal indices must be converted or re-measured to meet Indonesian category thresholds, and no automatic acceptance of Chinese baseline values is assumed.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for covered import categories under ESDM MEPS regime
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for domestic efficiency regimes; value basis differs from Indonesia

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] MEPS/EER compliance is a recurring gap area; Indonesian category thresholds and calculation method should be validated before import declaration and sales launch.

source.publisher: Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry (ESDM), Indonesia

rows.requirement: KLHK ODS/HFC phase-down controls for refrigerants
rows.target_requirement: KLHK applies refrigerant management tied to ODS/HFC controls for import and in-market operation. Indonesia-specific handling includes refrigerant phase-down planning, reporting and control practices that align with national implementation pathways. R-22 is subject to phase-down transition constraints and legacy import/product controls must be verified per model and charge level.
target_standards: KLHK import and import-equipment refrigerant guidance
rows.china_equivalent: China participates in global ODS/HFC reduction frameworks and applies refrigerant standards including GB safety and labeling norms, but product-level administrative licensing and enforcement sequences are not identical for Indonesian imports.
rows.gap: For Indonesian-bound models, relying solely on Chinese refrigerant test reports is risky. Import teams should separately confirm KLHK expectations for refrigerant class, charge declaration, and phase-down compliance status.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where KLHK ODS/HFC licensing or declaration applies to the imported model
mandatory_status.cn: Policy-controlled under China ODS/HFC paths; administrative structure and evidence not equivalent

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Refrigerant controls are likely a binding gap until KLHK product-level and model-level status is confirmed for each shipment.

source.publisher: Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK), Indonesia

rows.target_requirement: Indonesia follows refrigerant transition direction where lower-GWP pathways are increasingly embedded in policy and import assessment. Products using R-32 or R-410A should be assessed against current transition guidance, product safety documentation, and any local labeling or registration additions requested by KLHK or associated agencies.
target_standards: KLHK refrigerant transition and compliance updates
KLHK product documentation and import screening
rows.china_equivalent: China also manages refrigerant phase-down through related ODS/HFC pathways and has technical transition practices, but Indonesia’s local transition checkpoints and required declarations are implemented through its own administrative stack.
rows.gap: Exporters should avoid assuming a one-to-one mapping between Chinese refrigerant planning and Indonesian acceptance. R-22 legacy stock, conversion kits, and service obligations should be reviewed against Indonesian transition logic.

mandatory_status.target: Expected to be mandatory where KLHK transition screening includes imported air-source heat pump models
mandatory_status.cn: China has related refrigerant controls but with different transition administration and evidentiary scope

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] No automatic equivalence is assumed for refrigerant transition status; KLHK transition documentation should be verified per model and refrigerant charge level before shipment.

source.publisher: Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK), Indonesia

rows.target_requirement: Indonesia references SNI harmonization paths for electrical safety and relies on BSN/JIS-referenced test baselines such as IEC 60335-2-40 in practice where air-source heat pumps and heat-pump-mode conditioners are assessed. Voltage/frequency compatibility is 220 V single-phase or 380 V three-phase at 50 Hz, which aligns with Chinese products for this product lane.
target_standards: BSN technical references for imported air appliances
rows.china_equivalent: China applies safety systems such as CCC and related GB safety standards for electrical goods, and shares 50 Hz operation but requires separate Indonesian safety evidence and marking for market access. Common test data cannot be presumed to satisfy Indonesia without review.
rows.gap: The major gap is regulatory format and marking evidence, not fundamental frequency/voltage compatibility. Ensure Indonesia-facing test/label dossiers and responsible-party alignment are prepared in addition to shared technical baseline checks.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where imported equipment and installation pathways are within Indonesian electrical safety scope
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory under China CCC for applicable domestic-market products; evidence does not automatically transfer

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Electrical safety appears administratively mandatory for market access; 50 Hz and 220/380 V alignment reduces electrical incompatibility risk but does not replace Indonesian compliance paperwork.

rows.requirement: Mandatory SNI certification and KEMENDAG pre-clearance
rows.target_requirement: Indonesia requires BSN-issued SNI certification before market entry, with KEMENDAG administrative obligations (including Pertek) applied for imports. Heat pumps and heat-pump-mode air conditioners must carry valid Indonesian documentation, and customs clearance should be supported by the Indonesian SNI route and marking requirements. KEMENDAG and BSN processes are market-entry gates, not post-sale advisories.
target_standards: KEMENDAG import procedures and Pertek for mandatory SNI products
rows.china_equivalent: China has a separate China baseline where GB/T 7725 and GB 25454 describe performance and testing, and CCC applies to heat pumps at or below 40 kW in domestic certification context, but CCC is not recognized for Indonesian customs and pre-clearance.
rows.gap: Primary gap is evidence transfer: Chinese CCC and GB documents do not satisfy Indonesian SNI customs pre-clearance by themselves. Importers need Indonesia-facing certificates, marking, and responsible-party processes before clearance and sale.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for SNI-listed imported products before market access and customs clearance
mandatory_status.cn: Mandatory in China for categories under CCC; not equivalent for Indonesia entry

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] SNI and Pertek-facing compliance is required for Indonesian import readiness; Chinese CCC/G/T evidence should be treated as source reference only, not clearance evidence.

source.publisher: Badan Standardisasi Nasional (BSN), Ministry of Trade (KEMENDAG), Indonesia
